claims.text: The as-synthesized PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles are a homogeneous solid solution.
The as-synthesized PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles have a uniform surface composition.
Mild thermal annealing selectively segregates Pt to the surface of PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles.
Pt surface segregation increases the density of Pt-rich surface sites.
Increasing the Pt surface concentration enhances adsorption and activation of ethanol and its intermediates.
A favorable surface electronic environment and adsorption of key intermediates can facilitate electron transfer during electrocatalysis.
Pt surface enrichment reduces activation-energy barriers for ethanol oxidation.
The increased density of Pt-rich sites enhances ethanol oxidation activity.
Annealed catalysts will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current densities than untreated catalysts.
Annealed catalysts will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation turnover frequencies than untreated catalysts.
Annealing may modify ethanol-oxidation product selectivity.
HEA nanoparticles can retain structurally similar solid-solution configurations over elevated temperatures.
A mild annealing window exists in which Pt segregation occurs without significant sintering or loss of the PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution phase.
Ambient-pressure XPS can be used to compare the surface Pt concentration of annealed and untreated catalysts.
Failure to increase surface Pt, failure to enhance activity, or failure to change selectivity would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Selectivity modification is described only as a potential outcome, but the falsification rule treats the absence of a selectivity change as independently sufficient to falsify the activity-centered hypothesis.
